newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Government's majority under pressure - NZ Herald.
newsitem.headline: Government's majority under pressure - NZ Herald.

text.p: The government is making preliminary inquiries about the consequences of a by-election in Te Tai Hauauru -- the seat held by beleaguered New Zealand First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan, the New Zealand Herald reported on Wednesday.

It is not necessarily expecting another vote so soon after the general election, but has assigned a senior minister, Doug Graham, to find out the details of the law if one is forced by the unfolding saga of Aotearoa Television Network, which Morgan helped to set up. The stakes are high, the paper reports.
"At risk is the coalition government's one seat parliamentary majority, which would be lost if the seat returned to Labour."
The Coalition Government holds 61 seats in the 120-seat parliament.
Some NZ First Party members believed that if Morgan resigned the party would be entitled to one more seat because of the percentage of votes it received in the 1996 election.
But chief executive of the Electoral Commission Paul Harris confirmed that the Electoral Act does not allow for a top-up and the House would remain at 120 seats.
Morgan is preparing a defence brief to present to his caucus on Tuesday.
By that time the Ministry of Commerce report into Aotearoa Television will be published. The Serious Fraud Office is also investigating and will not say when it expects to be finished its inquiries.
